pillar_reactions.evidence: Call terminated at five minutes; nothing about the programme was delivered.
Never raised, though the rep gestured at the logic — 'we can give you a routine, but if you can[not] stick to it, then you're still going to get injured.'

anchors.raw: I just want to get, like, a workout routine. And I just like what I saw. I need, like, a more functional workout routine.
anchors.note: He came to buy a routine, which in this market is a $30-$200 digital product, not a six-month $6,000 coaching relationship. Paired with 'I just figured it would be an online thing and pricing and that', he arrived expecting a checkout page and got a 45-minute qualification call. That mismatch, not the price, is what he balked at — and nothing in the call ever reframed what was actually for sale.

unmet_demand.want: A functional workout routine he can buy off a page, with the price shown up front
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is a six-month coached programme sold through a discovery call, with price disclosed only after a fit conversation — the exact structure he objected to. The rep confirmed the constraint rather than bridging it: 'I can give you the price, but eventually it's not going to be a good fit if we don't know if we can help you.'

unmet_demand.want: To stop getting injured every one to two months of training
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never explored. The injury cycle is the thing the programme's mobility and form-correction pillar exists to address, and it was surfaced and abandoned inside sixty seconds without anyone establishing what the injuries even are.
